expanded-1280-n293: the two columns line up correctly at 1280. Each English verse (justified, left) sits level with its Hebrew line (right-aligned, ragged left) in all 23 visible pairs. The inline ↗ source links appear in both languages (e.g. 'hairy ↗hands', '↗in captivity' matching ↗שעירות and ↗ונלוה). There is no clipping, and the spacing around those links looks normal.

expanded-1280-n309: the instruction pair does not sit side by side. The Hebrew instruction 'חזן' / 'כשנושאים כפיים, הש״ץ אומר את המילה כהנים בקול.' spans full width at right (y≈95–123), and the English 'When there is a priestly blessing, the cantor says the word Kohanim aloud.' comes after it at left (y≈151). The result is readable and the word spacing is normal ('Kohanim aloud', 'הש״ץ'), so this looks like the intended full-width instruction style rather than a defect. The standalone 'חזן' label has no English equivalent, which fits the colophon note that no translations were added for passages missing from the English edition.

verdict: Approved for the expanded HTML tail. In all four screenshots the columns line up and are readable at 1280, the mobile layout stacks correctly at 390, the inline source links and colophon attribution are present, instruction spacing is normal, and nothing is clipped beyond the expected sticky-header overlap. The browser summary reports no errors, duplicate IDs, broken internal links or overflow. The findings above are cosmetic or limits of what these screenshots can show.
